steps.description:
In mechatronics and robotics, controlling motors accurately is crucial because it helps machines move smoothly, in the right direction, and at the right speed, even when they have to move several parts at the same time.

The Motor block is used to control the turning of the wheels.



The following are some examples of movement when different speeds are applied to each wheel.


Place 2 obstacles in your virtual robot space as shown below. Using Motor blocks, navigate your virtual robot to make a U-turn while avoiding the obstacles.

  

The obstacle positions and your path should be similar but do not need follow exactly.

Move straight, make a turn and move straight again. Keep the speed low for easier control.

The Motor block is used to control the turning of the wheels.



Negative speeds cause the wheels to reverse. The following are some examples of movement when different speeds are applied to each wheel.

    


Place 2 obstacles in your virtual robot space as shown below. Using Motor blocks, navigate your virtual robot to make a 3-point turn while avoiding the obstacles. 


The obstacle positions and your path should be similar but do not need follow exactly.

The Motor block is used to control the turning of the wheels.


Negative speeds cause the wheels to reverse. The following are some examples of movement when different speeds are applied to each wheel.

    


Place 3 obstacles in your virtual robot space as shown below to form a triangle. Using Motor blocks, navigate your virtual robot to make pass through each obstacle. One of the obstacles must be at the start position of your vehicle. You can adjust the other two such that you can use Repeat loop to navigate through the triangle (need not be exact).



Try out the experiment below (but you do not need to submit it):

  • Navigate the triangle 10 times. Unless your path is perfectly accurate, your robot will drift farther and farther from the targets due to accumulating errors. Small imprecisions can snowball into big problems!
